name: Pricing Divergence Matrix

divergence_cases.difference: Incompatible request structure; Engine A takes flat screen array + optional time windows, Engine B takes structured items array without intraday window support
divergence_cases.target_architecture: Engine A is Canonical Domain Engine; Engine B is isolated behind LegacyPricingEngineAdapter

divergence_cases.engine_a_behavior: Resolves attached PricingPlan, evaluates duration tiers, screen tiers, and calculates exact runtime hours
divergence_cases.engine_b_behavior: Takes base_price from screen or plan; if monthly rate exists divides by 30, if weekly divides by 7
divergence_cases.difference: Engine A supports dynamic pricing rules and intraday scheduling; Engine B uses simple calendar division

engine_a: Marketplace advertiser campaigns, partner campaigns, manual bookings

divergence_cases.target_architecture: Preserve existing algorithms in their respective domains; do not force unification without product sign-off

divergence_cases.engine_a_behavior: Evaluates calendar day of week and intraday runtime hour overlaps with plan peak_hours; applies percentage charges per day
divergence_cases.engine_b_behavior: No concept of peak hours or weekend surcharges; flat calculation across all days
divergence_cases.difference: Engine A adds peak/weekend charges to subtotal; Engine B ignores day-of-week and time-of-day pricing variations
divergence_cases.target_architecture: Engine A maintains peak/weekend domain rules; Engine B remains isolated

divergence_cases.engine_a_behavior: Evaluates PricingPlanDuration rules configured per screen (e.g. 7-day, 14-day, 30-day tiered percentages)
divergence_cases.engine_b_behavior: Hardcoded flat 10% discount applied strictly if total duration >= 30 days
divergence_cases.difference: Engine A uses database-driven multi-tier rules; Engine B uses hardcoded 10% threshold
divergence_cases.target_architecture: Retain separate rule application to preserve 100% contract fidelity for existing clients

divergence_cases.engine_a_behavior: Supports referral codes (percentage or flat), first-booking discount for new users, and loyalty point redemption
divergence_cases.engine_b_behavior: Does not support promotional codes, partner referrals, first-booking incentives, or loyalty points
divergence_cases.difference: Engine A supports the full commercial incentive layer; Engine B is pure inventory quotation
divergence_cases.target_architecture: Incentive layer is part of Canonical CampaignPricingEngine

divergence_cases.engine_a_behavior: Returns { campaign_summary, per_screen: [{ daily_breakdown: [...] }], aggregated: { base_price, screen_discount, duration_discount, combined_discount, peak_adjustment, weekend_adjustment, subtotal_before_discount, subtotal_after_discount, first_booking_discount, referral_discount, reward_discount, final_total } }
divergence_cases.engine_b_behavior: Returns { summary: { total_items, total_quantity, start_date, end_date, duration_days }, line_items: [...], pricing: { gross_total, discount_total, final_total, daily_average } }
divergence_cases.difference: Completely different JSON schema and keys; client applications depend on exact response keys

engine_a: Frontend campaign builder, partner booking portal

divergence_cases.target_architecture: Preserve both response structures exactly as defined in API contracts

decision_summary: Do NOT unify or merge Engine A and Engine B. Engine A is extracted into App\Domain\Pricing\CampaignPricingEngine as the canonical marketplace engine. Engine B is wrapped in App\Application\Pricing\Adapters\LegacyPricingEngineAdapter to preserve 100% backward compatibility for /api/v2/pricing/calculate.
